summary: Arinde L. Jonker is an Indologist who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied under MA supervisor Peter C. Bisschop and teacher Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
Aritri Dutta is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied as an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under the supervision of Henk Blezer (attested 2026).

Arjo Vanderjagt is a scholar of philosophy and history. After studying at the University of Groningen (1971–1981), he held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1999–2004) under Henk Bodewitz. He held posts at the University of Groningen (~2003–2005) and has served as professor at EFEO since 2008.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian and Indologist. He completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (1779–1784) under Heyne and Spittler, later serving there as Privatdozent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).

Arnold J. Toynbee was a historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1907–1911). He held academic posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He served as Deputy Professor of Sanskrit at Corpus Christi College (~1888–1899) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford starting in 1888.

Arthur Berriedale Keith was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Macdonell and Eggeling. He worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) and was professor at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Burks was a philosopher and computer scientist. He studied at DePauw University and the University of Michigan, completing his studies under Cooper Harold Langford (~1937–1941), and served as a professor at Michigan (~1946–1986).

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London (~1857–1860) under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Fausbøll and Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880).

Arthur Emanuel Christensen was a scholar of Iranian studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1903) and under F. C. Andreas. He held Copenhagen's first chair of Oriental studies (1919–1945).
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright was a historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard. He taught at Stanford University (1947, professor in 1958) before becoming Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale (1959, 1961).

Arthur Hilary Armstrong was a philosopher who studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. He held academic positions at Swansea, the University of Malta, Cardiff, and served as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).
Arthur John Evans was an archaeologist and historian who was educated at Harrow School (~1865–1870) and Brasenose College (1870).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held professorships at SOAS (1957–1965) and the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

Arthur Philip McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), studying under Parimal G. Patil, Pelri Sanggye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena. He studied under Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf in Berlin, where he later held a dozentur and post at the university (~1820–1831).

Arthur Venis was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1881 and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad.
